title: WorkflowSpec
description: A whole workflow. `entrypoint` is the ordered list of top-level nodes to run (matches mloky's model). `nodes` is the id → node map.

host.description: Optional host wiring (prompts, schemas, viz). Not part of replay identity.

BudgetCap.description: One declared cap on a run.

hard.description: When true, exceeding the cap fails the run if [`BudgetPlan::fail_on_hard_exhaust`].

label.description: Optional display name (panel + snapshot). Defaults to [`BudgetKind::as_str`].

show_eta.description: Include this cap on the ETA viz line when a forecast exists (default true).

show_progress.description: Include this cap on the progress viz line (default true).

warning_percent.description: Per-cap warning threshold override (percent of cap). Falls back to plan default.

BudgetEtaConfig.description: ETA / burn-rate forecast knobs (host metering + engine).

enabled.description: Master switch for ETA forecasting (default true).

min_wall_secs.description: Minimum wall seconds before burn-rate ETA is trusted (default 1.0).

mode.description: Which ETAs to surface on the panel.

sample_interval_secs.description: Host sampling cadence hint for live follow (default 0.45s).

BudgetEtaMode.description: How ETA lines are composed on the terminal panel.

oneOf.description: Do not show or compute ETA forecasts.
Show every cap that has a finite forecast (default).
Impure actor invocations (model turns, env-coupled hero acts, …).
Total tokens (in+out) observed on the live bus / recorded usage.
Wall-clock seconds since the host started the run.

BudgetPlan.description:
Full budget configuration for a workflow run (part of [`crate::topology::RunPlan`]).

This is the **typed JSON interface**: serialize/deserialize as `runplan.budgets`.

caps.description: Caps by dimension. Empty plan ⇒ no metering / no panel lines.

fail_on_hard_exhaust.description: Fail the run when a `hard` cap is exhausted (default true).

warning_percent.description: Default warning threshold as percent of cap (0–100). Default 80.

BudgetVizConfig.description: Terminal / panel rendering knobs for budgets.

enabled.description: Master switch (default true). When false, no budget lines are drawn.

short_labels.description: Use short labels (`calls`/`tok`/`wall`) instead of full kind names.

GoalPlan.description:
Full goal configuration for a workflow run (part of [`crate::topology::RunPlan`]).

This is the **typed JSON interface**: serialize/deserialize as `runplan.goals`.

cancel_in_flight.description: Future control-plane knob: when true, hosts/runners may cancel queued in-flight map work after success wrap-up. Default false preserves v1 entrypoint-skip semantics.

fail_on_unmet.description: Fail the run when a `required` goal is still unmet at run end. Default true.

finalize.description: Optional finalize node id to run on success wrap-up. Recorded in v1; runner wiring is a follow-up (see `docs/GOALS.md`).

goals.description: Declared goals. Empty plan ⇒ no evaluation / no panel line.

terminate_on_met.description: When every required goal is met, allow the runner to skip remaining entrypoints (early success wrap-up). Default true.

GoalSpec.description: One declared goal on a run.

oneOf.description: Met when the ledger value at `path` deep-equals `equals`.
Met when the numeric ledger value at `path` is `>= min`. Progress = `value/min`.

label.description: Optional display name (panel + snapshot). Defaults to [`Self::id`].

required.description: Required goals gate the run state and `fail_on_unmet` (default true). Non-required goals record progress only and never block.

show_progress.description: Include this goal on the progress viz line (default true).

GoalVizConfig.description: Terminal / panel rendering knobs for goals.

enabled.description: Master switch (default true). When false, no goal line is drawn.

short_labels.description: Use short labels (goal id) instead of the full label.

show_progress.description: Show the per-goal progress line (`goals 1/2 met · quality 0.72/0.80`).

GroundingPlan.description: Declared grounding requirements for a run (`runplan.grounding`).

trace_required.description: When TRUE, every recorded output must be graded from a READ trace body; any ungraded or unread row degrades the run's [`GroundingReport`] to [`GroundingStatus::RequiredTraceUnread`] — independently of [`crate::artifact::RunStatus`].

HostConfig.description: Host-side wiring for a workflow: actor prompts, output schemas, and viz hints. Optional on [`WorkflowSpec`]; reference workloads may also supply defaults via the linked workload crate. The core runner never reads this — only the host.

output_schemas.description: Actor name → JSON Schema path (relative to the spec dir).

roles.description: Actor name → role prompt (inline or file path relative to the spec dir).

sandboxes.description: Actor name → sandbox declaration (seeded workspace the actor runs in). Host-only, like the rest of `HostConfig`; honored by `jesterky-sandbox`.

viz.description: Live terminal viz hints (item preseed, matrix field, map node label).

HostRole.description: How the host configures one actor's system prompt.

prompt_file.description: Path relative to the workflow spec file's directory.

HostVizConfig.description: Host hints for live follow / post-run matrix display.

item_jobs_field.description: Array field on that program's output (default `jobs`).

item_labels_op.description: Program op whose output supplies item labels before the map starts.

map_node.description: Map node id for viz preseed when no events have arrived yet.

matrix_report_field.description: Recorded-output field to print after a completed follow run.

Limit.description: A named concurrency budget. Enforced by the runner; `permits` bounds how many holders may hold it at once.

Node.description: A node = its kind plus its I/O wiring.

oneOf.description: Pure, deterministic, in-process op (e.g. `quality.expand`). Re-run on replay — NOT recorded (ADR #7). Resolved from the program registry.
Pure aggregation over a collection (a program that folds `results`).
A host actor call (a model, a subprocess). Impure → recorded for replay.

Fan `body` over `over`, binding each element as `item_as`. `concurrency` opts into parallel execution (ADR #5); `None`/`1` = serial. `min_success` is the reduce-gate (fraction of items that must succeed).
Serial iteration with side effects visible across items.
Loop `body` while `cond` resolves truthy, bounded by `max_iters`. Each pass increments the `Addr::iteration` at this node.

Spawn one session per element of `sessions`, each running `body` against the named `actor`. `limit` (permits) serializes shared-resource access — this is the "poll under a center logic" pattern (DungeonGrid): set `permits = 1` on the env resource so sessions take turns.
Resume a previously-checkpointed session and run `body`.

inputs.description: Inputs the node reads, resolved from the ledger before it runs.

outputs.description: Outputs the node writes back into the ledger when it completes.

Ref.description: A reference into run state, resolved by the ledger at execution time. Kept a newtype over String in the skeleton; M0 replaces the inner form with a parsed `{ source, path }` so resolution is total and checkable.

RunPlan.description: Run-level configuration: concurrency budgets, resource budgets, and event verbosity. A run may override these via args.runplan (merged by the runner).

budgets.description: Formal **resource** budgets (actor calls / tokens / wall seconds) with progress + ETA. See [`crate::budget`].

goals.description: Formal **goals / work products** (semantic termination targets) — the dual of [`Self::budgets`]. See [`crate::goal`].

grounding.description: Declared **annotation grounding** requirements (evidence quality), separate from lifecycle. See [`crate::grounding`]. Skipped when empty so pre-existing specs keep their `spec_hash` (replay identity).

limits.description: Named **concurrency** limits → permits (semaphores). A `map` / `session_group` `limit` names one of these. Distinct from [`Self::budgets`].

map_concurrency.description: Default parallel width for `map` nodes lacking their own `concurrency`. `None`/`1` = serial (ADR #5).

SandboxBackend.description: Where the actor executes. `Local` = a host temp dir with the host toolchain; `Docker` = codex runs INSIDE the named container (image toolchain, isolated).

env.description: Env exported to the actor's process inside the container (e.g. `CODEX_HOME=/codex-home`). Overrides the actor's own env for that key.

mounts.description: Extra bind mounts as docker `-v` specs, `host:container[:ro]`. `${HOME}` and `$VAR` are expanded. This is how codex auth reaches the container: mount host `~/.codex` to an in-container path, then point `CODEX_HOME` there via [`Self::Docker::env`].

setup.description: Commands baked/run at container start before the actor (e.g. warm caches).

SandboxCapture.description: What to read back out of the workspace after the actor finishes, and where to put it in the actor's outputs so downstream nodes can consume it.

globs.description: Globs relative to the workspace root (e.g. `["Cargo.toml", "src/**/*.rs"]`).

into.description: Output field to hold the captured `{files:[{path,content}]}`.

SandboxConfig.description: Per-actor sandbox declaration (keyed by actor name in `HostConfig.sandboxes`).

network.description: Whether the actor's tools may reach the network. Off by default.

SandboxMode.description: The permission level the actor should self-apply (maps to codex `--sandbox`).

oneOf.description: Read the workspace, run nothing that writes it. Default — least privilege.
Create/modify files and run builds/tools in the workspace.

SandboxSeed.description: How the workspace is populated before the actor runs. All three compose, in order: write `files_input`, copy `copy_from`, run `setup`.

copy_from.description: Host dirs copied into the workspace root (paths relative to the spec dir).

files_input.description: Ledger input field holding `{files:[{path,content}]}` written to the workspace — lets an upstream node produce the workspace contents.

setup.description: Commands run once after seeding (e.g. `uv sync`).
